cards.title: Google DeepMind Launches Gemini 4 Carbon: #1 on AA Intelligence Index v5 with Cybersecurity SOTA
cards.why_it_matters: A new flagship frontier model from DeepMind ranking first on the most prominent independent intelligence index—with major jumps in agentic coding and cybersecurity—is a must-know development for anyone tracking frontier capabilities.
cards.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon scores 59 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, ranking #1. It achieves SOTA on SEC-bench Pro (88.2% vulnerability finding), ExploitGym (54.8% exploitation), and CWE-bench (71.0% patching). It jumps +89 Elo to #4 on WebDev Arena (1768). Priced at $2/M input and $10/M output tokens, Carbon is initially rolling out only to select cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program before broader release.

cards.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe: Open-Weight Model for Multilingual ASR, Diarization, and Audio Q&A
cards.why_it_matters: A single open-weight checkpoint topping the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard for English and two speaker-attribution benchmarks is directly relevant if you work on speech pipelines or need promptable, adaptable transcription infrastructure.
cards.summary: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, promptable model handling transcription (40 languages), translation (31 languages to/from English), speaker attribution (13 languages, up to 8 speakers, up to 1-hour recordings), and audio Q&A in one checkpoint. It leads the HF Open ASR Leaderboard (English), posts the lowest error rate on David AI's 21-language diarization leaderboard, and ranks first in VoiceArena's 14-system comparison. Fine-tuning on medical audio cut WER 45.8% relative to best-prompt baseline.

cards.title: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5: Benchmark Design Under the Microscope
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI/ML engineer who relies on leaderboards to compare models, understanding how AA's flagship index is constructed—and where it strains—directly affects how you interpret frontier model rankings.
cards.summary: AA's v5 Intelligence Index splits evenly across Knowledge Work, Coding, Science, and General (25% each), using tasks like FrontierCode 2.0, Terminal-Bench, and HLE-Diamond. The author critiques aggregation trade-offs, notes that v5 places 8 closed models above the best open-weight contender (Kimi K3.1 Pro), and argues singular intelligence indices are increasingly ill-suited to jagged, rapidly advancing frontier capabilities.
